historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: nominal mid-cycle growth (volume ~1% + price ~1%); trailing CAGRs are cycle artefacts
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Trailing CAGRs are not usable as a growth anchor. FY2025 EPS (-3.70) and owner FCF (reported -1,447 less SBC 385) are negative, so EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined; the 3-year window starts at the FY2022 peak (revenue 56,902) and the 5-year window starts at the FY2020 pandemic low, so revenue reads -11.1% and +0.7% and equity -6.2% and +6.1% for the same business. Equity 5yr CAGR diverges >30% from revenue.
historical_growth.notes: Annual FY2020-FY2025 from Metrics.csv. Owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC incl. equity-award taxes): FY2020 4,776, FY2021 5,220, FY2022 5,406, FY2023 2,586, FY2024 -225, FY2025 -1,832. Operating EBITDA: FY2022 9,348, FY2023 5,389, FY2024 5,482, FY2025 3,256, 9M-2026 4,738.

scenario_narratives.base: The 2026 earnings rebound is partly borrowed: local price rose 14-20% on Middle East / Hormuz supply disruption while volume fell. As that normalises in 2027, spreads give back some of the gain and self-help (Transform to Outperform plus the 2025 structural programme) fills part of the hole, leaving Operating EBITDA near 5.5bn. A genuine polyethylene and polyurethane operating-rate recovery arrives around 2028-2030 as capacity additions slow, lifting margins to 15% before settling at a 14.5% mid-cycle level -- roughly half of the ~3bn of cost savings retained, the rest competed away as it usually is in commodity chains. Alberta Path2Zero is built on its 2029 schedule, holding capex above D&A until then. The dividend stays at $1.40 and the balance sheet stays investment grade.
scenario_narratives.bull: The disruption-era pricing proves stickier because high-cost European and Asian naphtha capacity is permanently closed, the cycle turns in 2027-2028 as consensus hopes, and Dow keeps most of the >3bn self-help. Mid-cycle Operating EBITDA margin returns to 17% -- the 2019 level -- with a 2030-31 peak of 18%, AI/data-centre, electronics and silicones demand adds volume above GDP, and Alberta starts up on time and on budget with ethane-advantaged, low-carbon tonnes. This needs the cycle, the cost programme and the project to all deliver.
scenario_narratives.bear: Overcapacity is structural rather than cyclical: Chinese and Middle Eastern polyethylene and polyurethane capacity keeps arriving, the 2026 price spike reverses fully once Gulf supply normalises, and the US ethane advantage narrows. Revenue falls 9% in 2027 and margins revisit 2025-style levels (9.5-10%) before recovering only to 12% -- below even the 2023-24 experience net of cost savings that are competed away. Capex is cut and Alberta is slowed again, the Sadara guarantee is called, and with net debt near 13bn against ~4.5bn of EBITDA the rating slips to high yield and the dividend is cut a second time. In this path the equity is worth little after debt, pensions and minorities: the claims ahead of the common absorb nearly all of enterprise value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Dow is valued on normalised, through-the-cycle unlevered owner free cash flow, not on either the FY2025 trough or the disruption-flattered FY2026 run-rate. The equity is a thin residual: enterprise value must clear ~12.8bn of net debt and ~8bn of minorities, pension, guarantee, asbestos and restructuring claims before a dollar reaches the common, so per-share value is highly geared to the mid-cycle margin assumption -- each 1pp of mid-cycle Operating EBITDA margin is worth several dollars a share. That gearing is the main finding: the range between bear and bull is wide and the weighted value should be read as the centre of a broad distribution.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle Operating EBITDA margin (14.5% base) is the dominant driver; the 2023-2025 average was ~11% and the 2019-2025 average ~15% only because of the 2021-22 super-peak
How much of the 2026 price rebound is disruption-driven (Middle East / Hormuz) rather than a durable operating-rate recovery
Retention of the >3bn of announced self-help versus pass-through to customers in oversupplied chains
Sustainable capex: history ran at ~0.73x D&A; the model assumes ~0.97x in the terminal year plus the Alberta Path2Zero build through 2029
Claims ahead of the equity are estimates: NCI is taken at transaction-implied fair value (3.4bn vs 1.5bn book), the Sadara guarantee at 50% of 1.2bn
Terminal value is capped at 14x unlevered owner FCF, a cyclical-appropriate multiple that sits below what the market currently pays on depressed cash flow

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 20.93-42.74
data_sources.financials: DOW_Metrics.csv and DOW.duckdb kpis (Operating EBIT, segment EBIT, D&A, SBC, equity-award taxes); Q3 2026 Form 10-Q (balance sheet, cash flow, net debt table, Sadara guarantee, restructuring cash costs, capex guidance); FY2025 Form 10-K (pension funded status, asbestos, Operating EBITDA reconciliation)

inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares, Q3 2026 10-Q (727.4m; period-end basic 723.9m = 791.9m issued less 68.0m treasury). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. Dow has repurchased nothing since 2024 and the count has drifted up ~1.5%/yr via treasury issuances to compensation and benefit plans, so the flat count is a modelling convention the company is not currently funding.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 30 Sep 2026: cash-flow-statement SBC FY2025 367 - 9M-2025 293 + 9M-2026 261 = 335, plus employee taxes paid for share-based payment arrangements 18 - 16 + 15 = 17 (financing activities). Dow publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity ~10.4% (risk-free ~4.4% + beta 1.2 x 5.0% ERP); after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (BBB-/Baa3 paper at ~6% pre-tax); 65/35 target equity/debt gives ~8.3%, rounded to 8.5%. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality and leverage risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating lease cost is already an operating expense inside Operating EBITDA, so no lease line is added and operating lease liabilities (1,369) are excluded from net debt. Finance lease obligations sit inside reported long-term debt and are therefore in net debt. One treatment, charged once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are fully consolidated; noncontrolling interests are deducted once, in the equity bridge, at an estimated fair value of 3,400 rather than the 1,479 book value (InfraPark paid 2,943 for 49% of Diamond Infrastructure Solutions in 2025; NCI income is running ~315/yr and distributions ~350/yr).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the cyclical adaptations (routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'). Dow is a capital-intensive commodity/specialty chemicals producer whose value is a stream of unlevered free cash flow; no bank/REIT/holdco feature applies. First valuation of this ticker. CYCLE JUDGMENT: FY2025 (Operating EBITDA 3,256, 8.1% margin) was the trough; FY2026 is NOT a clean recovery year. 9M-2026 Operating EBITDA of 4,738 includes a Q2 spike (Operating EBIT 1,648 on +30% P&SP local price) driven by Middle East / Strait of Hormuz supply disruption while volumes fell 1%. Neither year is capitalised. The base case fades the price spike in year 1 and converges on a mid-cycle Operating EBITDA margin of 14.5% -- above the 2023-2025 average (~11%) because roughly half of the ~3bn of announced self-help is assumed to stick, below the 2019-2025 average (~15%) because that average is carried by the 2021-22 super-peak (9.3-12.5bn) that structural Chinese and Middle Eastern overcapacity makes unlikely to repeat. FY0: base_revenue is FY2026E = 9M actual 33,153 + Q4 estimate ~10,900, so year 1 is FY2027; net debt is the 30 Sep 2026 balance, so Q4 2026 cash flow is not counted (small, conservative). last_fcf / reported_fcf are TTM to 30 Sep 2026 (FY2025 -1,447 less 9M-2025 -1,147 plus 9M-2026 2,446); the TTM figure is flattered by cash received on the Nova judgment, a 318 Canadian tax refund and customer advance payments on long-term supply contracts, and is not used as a projection base. INTEREST INCOME: not stripped -- Dow is a net debtor, and the model is unlevered (EBITDA-based), so interest income never enters the flows. EQUITY AFFILIATES: Operating EBITDA includes equity earnings ex significant items, so the 1,119 investment in nonconsolidated affiliates is NOT added to the bridge (matching-asset rule); other investments of 3,201 (largely captive-insurance and benefit-related assets) are also left out. SBC is small (~0.8% of revenue), so the house/street band is narrow. Price is a regular-session close.

base.narrative: Year 1 (FY2027) fades the 2026 disruption-driven price spike: revenue -4%, margin 13.0% versus ~14% in FY2026E, with self-help offsetting part of the spread give-back. Margin then climbs to 15.0% at the 2030-31 cycle high and settles at a 14.5% mid-cycle level. Capex runs above D&A through 2029 for the Alberta Path2Zero build, then at 5.8% of revenue against D&A of 6.0% (2019-2025 capex averaged ~4.5% of revenue, ~0.73x D&A, which is not sustainable indefinitely). Working capital consumes 15% of incremental revenue (receivables + inventory less payables is ~17% of sales). Cash tax 25%, in line with the normal effective rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: ~12.8bn of net debt plus ~8bn of other claims sits ahead of the equity, Moody's is at Baa3 with a negative outlook, and forecasters do not expect a cycle recovery before 2027-2028, so a prolonged trough has real balance-sheet consequences. Base at 50%: a partial, self-help-assisted normalisation is the central case. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs three independent things -- a cyclical upturn, retention of most cost savings and on-time delivery of a multi-billion-dollar project already delayed once.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
